title: Migrating RBAC to PBAC
subtitle: Strangler pattern for brownfield estates
content:
🌿 The Strangler Sequence

  1. Inventory: extract every inline check into a catalog (route → current rule). You cannot migrate what you cannot list. Start mechanical: rg -n "role|permit|allow|isAdmin|can[A-Z]" --type py --type js services/ | sort > authz-inventory.txt, then hand-triage into route → rule rows — the grep finds candidates, humans write the catalog.
  2. Shadow mode: deploy PDP beside the old checks; log agreements/disagreements without enforcing. Disagreements are your spec.
  3. Role-import: encode existing roles as policy first (RBAC-in-PBAC) — zero behavior change, full test harness.
  4. Attribute enrichment: add tenant/owner/MFA rules one invariant at a time, each with deny-tests.
  5. Cutover per route: flip enforcement route-by-route with instant rollback (bundle version pin).
  6. Delete the old code: the strangler is done only when inline checks are gone, not when the PDP exists.

⚠️ Brownfield Hazards

  • Hidden admin backdoors (if email == 'ceo@…') surface in shadow-mode diffs — decide explicitly, never silently port.
  • Role explosion becomes policy debt if you transliterate 400 roles 1:1 — collapse dimensions into attributes during import.
  • Dual-write tuples need an outbox, not a distributed transaction: share-actions write old ACL rows AND emit tuple-writes via transactional outbox; there is no XA across your DB and OpenFGA — design for at-least-once + reconciliation.
  • Enforcement outside services: stored procedures, BI semantic layers, and warehouse grants are not lintable service code — inventory them as out-of-scope enforcement with owners, or the strangler strangles nothing.
  • PII in shadow logs: shadow mode records real requests; allowlist what the diff pipeline keeps (subject id, action, resource id, verdict, policy id) and redact everything else (payloads, emails, tokens, free-text attributes) — or the migration creates its own breach.
  • Attribute-source cleanup: HR/IdP feeds, stale groups, and dead roles migrate too — or the new PDP faithfully enforces garbage.

📏 Done Criteria (Tolerance-Based, Not Zero-Based)

A long-tail estate will never show a literal zero diff. Exit instead on: inline authZ conditionals at zero in services (linted) with a risk-accepted inventory of out-of-scope enforcement; shadow diff below an agreed threshold on sampled production inputs with every residual exception named, owned, and expiry-dated; per-route rollback rehearsed; freeze windows and audit sign-off completed; old code deleted route-by-route. Numeric example: <0.1% disagree on 100k sampled prod requests over 7 days, zero disagree on deny→allow flips, ≤5 named exceptions each with owner + expiry — calibrate the numbers to your estate, then freeze them in the migration charter. Migration without deletion is just two systems to breach.

🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Compare RBAC transliteration vs attribute-collapsed policy on role count. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: What runs first in a safe RBAC→PBAC migration?

options.text: Inventory of every inline check + shadow-mode PDP logging diffs without enforcing
Deleting all old authorization code immediately
Flipping every route to enforce on day one

questions.explanation: Shadow diffs ARE the migration spec: every disagreement between old checks and new policy is the first strangler decision to make explicitly.

questions.question: Shadow mode shows the old code allows what new policy denies for the CEO's email. Correct move?

options.text: Treat as explicit decision: encode or reject the backdoor deliberately, with approvers
Silently port the backdoor into policy
Ignore all diffs and cut over anyway

questions.explanation: Hidden grants surface in diffs precisely so they get deliberate treatment. Silent ports preserve invisible privilege.

questions.question: You have 400 roles (region × seniority × type). How to import them?

options.text: Collapse dimensions into attributes; encode rules, not role enumerations
Delete all roles and allow everyone

questions.explanation: 1:1 transliteration preserves role explosion as policy debt. Import the roles, then collapse dimensions into attributes — import is the step, collapse is the goal.

questions.question: Why cut over route-by-route instead of big-bang?

options.text: Blast radius control + instant per-route rollback via bundle pin

questions.explanation: Per-route cutover bounds every failure and makes rollback a version pin, not a war room.

questions.question: When is the migration actually done?

options.text: Old checks deleted route-by-route; diff below threshold with owned exceptions; rollback rehearsed; sign-off complete
When the PDP is installed (old code still running)
When the PDP container image is pinned (necessary hygiene, not migration-done)

questions.explanation: Tolerance-based exit: literal zero-diff is unattainable on long-tail estates. Done = old path gone, residuals named/owned/expiry-dated, rollback rehearsed. Coexistence is two systems to breach.

questions.question: Import discovers thirty roles nobody can explain. Treatment?

options.text: Quarantine with deny-by-default replacements plus owner attestation before porting

questions.explanation: Unexplained roles are unexploded ordnance. Quarantine first; port only what an owner will sign for.

questions.question: A route does three different things and has no clean permission. Cutover approach?

options.text: Split the handler, or gate the narrow union with an expiry plus a refactor ticket

questions.explanation: Unmappable routes are design debt surfacing. Time-box the broad gate and pay down the split.

questions.question: Shadow diffs show 99% agreement. How do you treat the 1%?

options.text: As the entire migration spec — triage every disagreement explicitly

questions.explanation: Agreement is uninteresting; disagreement is the spec. The 1% contains every backdoor and every misunderstanding.
